status: DRAFT — PROPOSED for owner decision. Schema only: term definitions, origins, closure rules and the crosswalk onto bus_power_boundary_v1. It carries no power numbers and is not wired into abep_sim (wiring is a model change for the owner).
role: Decomposition of the archengine / ppu P_bus (the legacy trade view: load-plane terms plus POOLED converter and harness losses) and its term-by-term crosswalk onto the common bus-power boundary. The admissibility-bearing architecture-comparison ledger is the one produced by abep_sim/arch_boundary.py (function bus_power_ledger, BOUNDARY_VERSION 'bus_power_boundary_v1', schema schemas/architecture_comparison/bus_power_boundary_v1.json, lane_11_bus_boundary). This schema never redefines it and never replaces it: an architecture comparison is admissible only on the boundary ledger (CLAUDE.md admissibility). The id 'bus_power_ledger_v1' names this decomposition schema; its instances are called 'decomposition instances' to keep them apart from arch_boundary.bus_power_ledger outputs.

milestones.A: supplies the vocabulary and the crosswalk so a conditional selection can state P_bus conditions on the common boundary per architecture (numbers TBD; no absolute Hall numbers exist)
milestones.B: not supported alone: needs evidenced loads and efficiencies per boundary component (lane_20_ppu_magnet electrical closure), an admitted Hall transport closure for hall_discharge (credible set is empty), OD-L1/OD-L2 decided, and the second lens on this single-lens-v1 lane
milestones.C: the ledger set is listed as a Milestone C integration deliverable (docs/architecture_comparison/dossier/dossier.json, 'schemas/ledgers/'); reaching C needs instances produced from integrated designs for every mode (steady, startup, peak) with every term computed

architectures.note: the RF/ECR arms change ONLY the pre-ionization method; the Hall accelerator, feed state, cathode and bus boundary are common. archengine names (abep_sim/archengine.py:arch_name) that correspond: hall_only = 'hall_internal+hall+<neutralizer>', rf_hall = 'rf_icp+hall+<neutralizer>', ecr_hall = 'ecr+hall+<neutralizer>'. archengine 'helicon+hall' (rf converter plus axial field) and 'dc_discharge+hall' are not covered by v1 (BUS_POWER_BOUNDARY.md section 3).
architectures.source: component sets copied by name from abep_sim/arch_boundary.py COMMON_COMPONENTS / PREIONIZER_COMPONENTS at execution branch e15f66f; tests/test_ledger_schemas.py compares them with the module whenever it is present

boundary.definition: P_bus = all electrical power crossing the spacecraft-side DC boundary into the propulsion system: discharge + pre-ionizer + cathode + magnets + PPU losses + gas path (compressor, valves/flow control) + controls + thermal control (heaters) + any other propulsion load. Wording follows the CLAUDE.md admissibility rule for bus_power_boundary_v1.
boundary.plane: input terminals of the PPU converters on the regulated spacecraft bus (abep_sim/ppu.py:PPU.V_bus); matches loads['P_bus_W'] of abep_sim/ppu.py:PPU.loads as used by abep_sim/archengine.py:close_architecture
never_P_bus: absorbed RF or microwave power in the source plasma (abep_sim/plasma_devices.py:ECRSource.absorbed, RFSource.absorbed); the bus-side quantity is the DC converter output P_ion_W plus its conversion loss
Hall discharge-only power (I_d x V_d) reported alone
boundary.outside: solar-array generation, battery/PCDU round trip and bus distribution upstream of the propulsion input terminal, and SPACECRAFT-level housekeeping (spacecraft avionics, ADCS, communications, payload; abep_sim/mission_env.py:Spacecraft bus_housekeeping_W and eps_eff). Propulsion-side housekeeping (controller, PPU control, sensors, TM/TC interface) is INSIDE, as P_housekeeping = boundary component 'housekeeping'. abep_sim/mission_env.py:array_area_for sizes arrays from P_bus.
boundary.alignment: aligned to bus_power_boundary_v1 (present on the execution branch since a2a1396): same boundary plane (propulsion DC bus input terminal(s)), same inside/outside split. The boundary's component names and per-component loss convention take precedence; the term-by-term mapping is boundary_crosswalk below.

modes.steady: firing steady state; the only mode archengine close_architecture evaluates
modes.startup: cathode heater + keeper x1.5 + compressor spin-up x1.8 (abep_sim/ppu.py:load_modes 'startup'); not evaluated by archengine (gap G7)
modes.peak: maximum simultaneous draw (e.g. solar-max flow, Xe augmentation); no producer in archengine (gap G7)

value_record: as defined in subsystem_ledger_v1.value_record (value, unit, status, origin, evidence; null value unless status is computed)

terms.definition: DC output of the Hall anode supply at its load plane (discharge power I_d x V_d)
terms.superseded_by: discharge_power_W of an admitted transport-ensemble member's design Hall map (hallthruster_bridge/hall_map_schema_v1.json, abep_sim/hall_map.py:HallMap); the credible set is empty, so value is null (TBD)

terms.definition: accelerating-stage supply of non-Hall families screened by archengine (grids anode, MPD, PIT capacitor charger, electrothermal heater)
terms.origin: abep_sim/archengine.py:_propulsion P_acc_W (grids / mpd / pit / thermal branches)
terms.note: screening families only; CLAUDE.md rule 8 (no new propulsion families) applies. Not representable on bus_power_boundary_v1, which covers only the three Hall-accelerated architectures (BUS_POWER_BOUNDARY.md section 3, 'Not covered by v1')

terms.definition: DC output of the pre-ionizer supply (RF amplifier or ECR/microwave HV supply) into the source, when the architecture has one
terms.note: the 'jet' share appears only when jet power exceeds the accelerating supply (from_src in close_architecture); absorbed plasma power is not a bus term. On the boundary it is rf_source (rf_amp converter, architecture rf_hall) OR ecr_source (hv_mw converter, architecture ecr_hall), never both; the ECR resonance-field coil is ecr_magnet (see P_magnets), not part of this term

terms.definition: cathode/neutralizer supplies: keeper (LaB6), heater (startup), plasma-bridge source (air cathodes)
terms.note: archengine routes the LaB6 heater share through the keeper converter (steady total only). On the boundary it splits into cathode_keeper and cathode_heater; the split producer on the execution branch is abep_sim.cathode_integration (lane 19: keeper mode, heater, start-up transient). In an archengine-derived crosswalk instance the keeper-converter efficiency applies to both and the split is TBD

terms.origin: abep_sim/archengine.py:close_architecture P_mag (code constant for hall / nozzle / ECR architectures)
terms.note: archengine charges one 25 W code constant for the Hall circuit whether or not an ECR source is present, so the ECR resonance-field supply is indistinguishable (BUS_POWER_BOUNDARY.md section 6). On the boundary the term splits into hall_magnet (every architecture) and ecr_magnet (ecr_hall only; explicit 0 W / efficiency 1 for a permanent-magnet circuit). Load-side producer on the execution branch: abep_sim.magnet_power (lane PPUMAG)

terms.definition: valve actuation/holding and flow-controller power on both propellant paths (atmospheric valve, Xe valve/regulator)
terms.origin: TBD — requires valve and flow-controller selection for both propellant paths with holding/actuation power data

terms.definition: the 'aux' converter load that the code carries without naming its consumer
terms.note: counted so the archengine decomposition closes; it cannot be placed on bus_power_boundary_v1 until the owner assigns it to exactly one of flow_control or housekeeping (open decision OD-L1; BUS_POWER_BOUNDARY.md section 6 lists it as 'not attributable')

terms.definition: heater power (gas chamber, Xe tank/lines, electronics survival) set by the cold-case (eclipse) thermal solution
terms.origin: TBD — requires heater set-points and a heater-power derivation from the cold case of abep_sim/thermal.py:size_radiator (computed there, not converted into heater power)

terms.definition: propulsion-side housekeeping electronics: propulsion controller / PPU control electronics and sensors (boundary component 'housekeeping'; NOT spacecraft avionics or spacecraft housekeeping, which are outside)
terms.origin: abep_sim/ppu.py:PPU.loads (controller_W + sensors_W, code constants, included in P_bus_W and P_loss_W)

terms.definition: conversion losses of all PPU converters, P_in - P_out summed over converters (ppu.loads P_loss_W minus controller_W and sensors_W). Decomposition view only: it is a pooled term
terms.origin: abep_sim/ppu.py:PPU.loads (P_loss_W minus controller_W and sensors_W) with abep_sim/ppu.py:Converter.efficiency

terms.definition: resistive loss in the harness between the bus input terminal and each load plane. Decomposition view only: on bus_power_boundary_v1 the harness loss is inside each component's efficiency and is never a separate term
terms.origin: TBD — requires harness lengths, gauges and currents; abep_sim/ppu.py:PPU.mass sizes harness mass only

boundary_crosswalk.authority: abep_sim/arch_boundary.py (COMMON_COMPONENTS, PREIONIZER_COMPONENTS, REQUIRED_COMPONENTS, COMPONENT_DEFINITIONS, bus_power_ledger) and docs/architecture_comparison/power_boundary/BUS_POWER_BOUNDARY.md sections 3 and 6 (archengine discrepancy audit); read-only, resolved lazily, never imported by this lane
boundary_crosswalk.loss_convention: bus_power_boundary_v1 books every loss per component: P_bus_c = P_load_c / efficiency_c, P_loss_c = P_bus_c - P_load_c, where efficiency_c is the end-to-end bus-terminal-to-load-plane ratio at the operating point and includes that component's converter, filters, generator/matching/isolator and HARNESS. Adopted here for every boundary instance. The pooled P_PPU_losses and P_harness_losses of the decomposition view are NOT boundary components; they are distributed into the component efficiencies by the allocation rules below, and a boundary instance never carries them as additional terms.

hall_discharge.producer: an admitted transport-ensemble member's design Hall map (discharge_power_W); credible set empty, so TBD

hall_magnet.producer: abep_sim.magnet_power (load-side I^2 R from the Vyovrinda magnetic-circuit design; efficiency from docs/architecture_comparison/electrical_closure/electrical_closure_data_v1.json)
hall_magnet.requires: Vyovrinda magnetic-circuit design (own geometry and B(z)) and supply-efficiency evidence

cathode_keeper.archengine_status: included (LaB6 keeper converter; plasma-bridge cathodes via cathode_src)

cathode_heater.archengine_status: lumped into keeper (the heater converter gets no steady demand; ppu.load_modes is not called by archengine)
cathode_heater.requires: cathode operating data per mode (keeper/heater split)

flow_control.archengine_status: excluded (unless inside the unattributed 5 W aux)
flow_control.requires: valve and flow-controller selection for both propellant paths

compressor.archengine_status: included; same load plane (motor + drive losses inside the load)

thermal_control.requires: heater set-points and a heater-power derivation (gap G4)

housekeeping.archengine_status: partly included, mis-classed (controller_W + sensors_W added at the bus with no conversion loss and booked inside ppu_loss_control)

rf_source.archengine_status: included at the generator DC input; RF generation efficiency inside the source physics
rf_source.producer: abep_sim/archengine.py:_propulsion P_ion_W (design variable); boundary load plane is NET RF power at the coil feed, so the archengine value is a DC-input quantity and must be re-referenced (see load_plane_note)

ecr_source.archengine_status: included at the magnetron DC input; magnetron and feed efficiency inside the source physics
ecr_source.producer: abep_sim/archengine.py:_propulsion P_ion_W (design variable); re-reference as for rf_source

ecr_magnet.archengine_status: excluded / indistinguishable (one P_mag constant for Hall and ECR)
ecr_magnet.producer: abep_sim.magnet_power (electromagnet or permanent_magnet; a permanent-magnet circuit is 0 W, efficiency 1, explicit)
ecr_magnet.requires: owner choice permanent magnet vs electromagnet (BUS_POWER_BOUNDARY.md section 9, BND-Q3) and the ECR circuit design

boundary_crosswalk.load_plane_note: rf_source / ecr_source: archengine P_ion_W is the converter output into the generator (a DC quantity); the boundary load is the net RF/microwave power at the coupling structure, with the generator inside the efficiency. BUS_POWER_BOUNDARY.md section 6 gives the mapping (rf_source efficiency = eta_conv(rf_amp) x eta_dc_rf). The bus total is unchanged by this re-referencing.

not_on_boundary.P_accelerator_other: outside v1 (non-Hall screening families); a comparison containing it is not admissible on bus_power_boundary_v1
not_on_boundary.P_aux_unallocated: unattributed; must be assigned to exactly one of flow_control or housekeeping (OD-L1) before a boundary instance is formed from archengine output; until then such an instance is NOT_EVALUABLE
not_on_boundary.P_PPU_losses: pooled; distributed per converter (allocation rule A1)
not_on_boundary.P_harness_losses: pooled; distributed per component run (allocation rule A2)

allocation_rules.A1_converter_losses: the loss of converter k (ppu.loads detail[k]: P_in - P_out) goes entirely into the efficiency of the boundary component that owns k (ppu_converters above), efficiency_c = sum_k P_out_k / sum_k P_in_k over the converters of c; each converter belongs to exactly one component (tested), so each converter watt is booked once. Converters with no boundary owner ('aux' until OD-L1; 'mpd_hc', 'cap_charger', 'heater_main' outside v1) make the instance NOT_EVALUABLE on the boundary.
allocation_rules.A2_harness_losses: when a harness model exists, its loss per run is added to the owning component's P_bus_c inside efficiency_c; P_harness_losses is then zero in the boundary instance by construction. A decomposition instance that carries P_harness_losses > 0 and a boundary instance of the same point must satisfy sum_c P_loss_c = P_PPU_losses + P_harness_losses (checked, not gated here; PROPOSED).
allocation_rules.A3_housekeeping: controller_W + sensors_W are a LOAD of housekeeping (not a loss). archengine adds them at the bus with no conversion, so an archengine-derived crosswalk instance carries housekeeping efficiency 1 as a statement about the code, not about hardware (evidence class 'assumed', inherited from abep_sim/ppu.py:PPU constants).
allocation_rules.A4_no_double_count: a watt appears in a boundary instance exactly once: as P_load_c or inside P_loss_c of exactly one component. P_PPU_losses, P_harness_losses and the archengine key ppu_loss_control never appear as additional boundary items.

decomposition_view.identity: P_bus_W = sum of the load-plane terms (P_discharge, P_accelerator_other, P_preionizer, P_cathode, P_magnets, P_compressor, P_valves_control, P_aux_unallocated, P_thermal, P_housekeeping) + P_PPU_losses + P_harness_losses. This is what abep_sim/archengine.py:close_architecture closes against abep_sim/ppu.py:PPU.loads (P_bus = controller_W + sensors_W + sum_k P_out_k / eta_k); the harness term is absent from the code (TBD).
decomposition_view.residual: resid = (P_bus_W - sum_terms P_term_W) / P_bus_W, with P_bus_W taken from abep_sim/ppu.py:PPU.loads
decomposition_view.gate: |resid| <= 0.02 (abep_sim/archengine.py:close_architecture rejects the candidate as 'energy_ledger' otherwise; CLAUDE.md rule 4)
decomposition_view.gate_rel_tol_source: abep_sim/archengine.py:close_architecture ('if abs(resid) > 0.02'); code constant, verified by tests/test_ledger_schemas.py
decomposition_view.golden_comparison: near-zero ledger_resid values are compared with an absolute tolerance (CLAUDE.md gate 6)
decomposition_view.not_a_completeness_check: the archengine ledger closes by construction (BUS_POWER_BOUNDARY.md section 6, point 1): a missing consumer (flow_control, thermal_control, a separate heater, an ECR magnet) leaves resid at zero. Completeness is carried by the completeness flag, never by resid.

boundary_view.identity: P_bus_W = sum over REQUIRED_COMPONENTS[arch] of P_load_c / efficiency_c (bus_power_boundary_v1)
boundary_view.residual: residual_W = (sum_c P_load_c + sum_c P_loss_c) - sum_c P_bus_c, absolute, in W
boundary_view.gate: rounding-level: |residual_W| <= 1e-12 x max(sum_c P_bus_c, 1 W), else RuntimeError; enforced by abep_sim/arch_boundary.py (function bus_power_ledger), not by this schema
boundary_view.producer: abep_sim.arch_boundary.bus_power_ledger; this schema never recomputes a boundary ledger
boundary_view.note: the two gates are different on purpose: the 2 % relative gate belongs to the archengine decomposition, the rounding-level absolute gate to the boundary

closure.crosswalk_consistency: for the same architecture, operating point and mode, the decomposition P_bus_W and the boundary P_bus_W are reported side by side with their difference and its itemization (terms present in one view only, OD-L1 allocation). No tolerance is set by this lane: PROPOSED for owner decision (OD-L2).

completeness.rule: closure is reported with a completeness flag, never as complete while a term is TBD

values.CLOSED_ALL_TERMS: |resid| <= 0.02 and every applicable term has status computed
values.CLOSED_MODELED_TERMS_ONLY: |resid| <= 0.02 over computed/partial terms; at least one applicable term is TBD (list them in open_terms)
values.NOT_EVALUABLE: an applicable term is superseded (e.g. P_discharge while the Hall credible set is empty), or a crosswalk to the boundary is blocked (P_aux_unallocated unattributed, a converter with no boundary owner); no P_bus is reported

closure.cap_check: P_bus_W <= abep_sim/constants.py:RFPConstraints power_max_W is checked only on CLOSED_ALL_TERMS instances; on CLOSED_MODELED_TERMS_ONLY it is reported as a lower bound (missing TBD terms can only add power). Architecture comparison uses the boundary P_bus only.
closure.per_mode: the identity and gate apply to each mode separately (steady, startup, peak); a mode without a producer is status TBD, not copied from steady

instance_required_fields.architecture: one of hall_only | rf_hall | ecr_hall (plus the archengine arch_name abep_sim/archengine.py:arch_name when the instance is derived from archengine)
instance_required_fields.operating_point_ref: design variables x_* and gas-path state
instance_required_fields.terms: {term_id: value_record} for every term above (not_applicable with reason where the architecture lacks it)
instance_required_fields.ensemble_member_id: required when P_discharge is computed from an admitted member's design Hall map; null otherwise
instance_required_fields.boundary_crosswalk: {boundary component: {P_load_W, efficiency, P_bus_W} value_records} for REQUIRED_COMPONENTS[architecture], or null with the blocking reason (OD-L1, superseded hall_discharge, ...)
